summary: Phase 149O.19.4 -- HATP Mandatory Independent-Verification Certification Implementation Plan: implementation-plan-only phase (no src/pcae/** file modified; no contract file modified). Confirmed baseline via direct inspection: repo clean at entry, origin/main..HEAD=0, 149O.19.3R.1 completed/complete at 19ed7cab, HMIC-001 status FROZEN -- REPAIRED, INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED, B-149O.19.3-1 INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED CLOSED, hardcoded False ceiling unchanged, HATP production NOT READY, runtime Observed/observe/unavailable. Read the full live HMIC-001 v1.0 contract text directly (not trusting prior-phase tables) and mechanically extracted all 144 HMIC-REQ requirements, 12 CIVC invariants, and 32 attack scenarios, mapping every one to a concrete production owner, failure/behavior, test owner, and implementation wave in a new implementation plan document (docs/PHASE_149O_19_4_HATP_MANDATORY_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION_CERTIFICATION_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md). Researched existing repository-conventional patterns to reuse (HATPTrustStore.production()/_test_only_root, _atomic_write_json/_reject_symlink, _TIMESTAMP_PATTERN, _require_revoked_at_consistency, repository_identity.py's CRI Layer 1, hatp_bootstrap.py's resolve_canonical_deployment_root) via direct source inspection of hatp_mandatory_cutover.py, repository_identity.py, and hatp_bootstrap.py, and reviewed the 149O.19.1 architecture doc's own prior reasoning without blindly adopting its module names. Selected module architecture: a single new core module src/pcae/core/hatp_mandatory_certification.py (data model + canonical parsing Wave A, implementation/repository/deployment/contract identity derivation Wave B, protected store + locking Wave C, validation engine Wave D) mirroring hatp_mandatory_cutover.py's own monolithic single-module precedent, plus a separate, non-agent-reachable admin script scripts/hatp_certification_admin.py (create/activate/revoke ceremony, Wave E) never imported by cli.py or commands/agent.py. hatp_mandatory_cutover.py's False-to-validator wiring is isolated to a single Wave F. Resolved this plan's one genuinely novel authority-sensitive question -- future-HMIC-validator self-reference/circularity -- using the contract's own explicit precedent (HMIC-REQ-050 already includes hatp_mandatory_cutover.py, the file containing the readiness gate, as item 1 of its own frozen set) rather than an improvised default or a contract-repair STOP: introduced explicit Stop Condition W-1 requiring a dedicated future HMIC-001 v1.1 contract-amendment phase to add hatp_mandatory_certification.py to the frozen file set, independently verified, strictly before Wave F may replace the False literal with a live validator call. Proved the admin writer itself does not require frozen-set protection because the validation algorithm's steps 9-11 always re-derive implementation identity/contract versions/certification-id fresh and compare against the stored record rather than trusting it -- a compromised writer can at worst produce a record that fails to validate. Confirmed HMIC-REQ-063's import-shadowing/executed-code-binding residual limitation remains explicitly out of scope for v1.0, consistent with the frozen contract's own disposition, not silently solved by this plan. Built a complete 144-row requirement traceability table, 12-row CIVC traceability table, and 32-row attack traceability table, a production file forecast/ownership matrix, a per-wave test-module plan, and a stop-conditions table (5 restated HMIC/governing-prompt conditions plus the new W-1 gate), none of which block Waves A-E/G from proceeding once separately scoped, with only Wave F additionally gated on W-1. Added a new 20-test planning-completeness suite (tests/test_phase_149o_19_4_hmic_implementation_plan_completeness.py) that mechanically re-extracts the 144/12/32 counts directly from HMIC-001's live contract text (not from this plan's own prose) and asserts the plan's tables match exactly, checks every row has a non-empty owner/test-owner/wave, checks the file-ownership matrix and stop-condition/W-1 text are present, and independently confirms via two separate git-diff extraction methods that no src/pcae/** file and none of the 8 upstream contracts changed. Fast Green (.venv): 28 pre-existing/unrelated failures unchanged before/after (git stash -u A/B confirmed byte-for-byte identical failure set on the unmodified baseline), 5592->5612 passed (+20 matching the new suite exactly). No certification artifact, active-certification pointer, or revocation record created anywhere in the repository. No Cutover Record or activation marker created or modified. No real Class-B provisioning. No real HATP_MANDATORY activation occurred. B-149O.19.3-1 remains independently closed, unchanged. B-149O-1..4 verdict unchanged, carried forward: INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED CLOSED AT SYSTEM IMPLEMENTATION/ENFORCEMENT BOUNDARY -- DEPLOYMENT/OPERATIONAL ACTIVATION DEFERRED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. Plan verdict: HMIC-001 IMPLEMENTATION PLAN: COMPLETE -- READY FOR BOUNDED IMPLEMENTATION. Recommended next phase: 149O.19.5A -- HMIC Certification Data Models + Canonical Parsing.
